# Quant experiments

Every experiment in the quants subproject, planned or done, so that nothing is run twice. Check this page before
starting anything; add a row before an experiment starts and fill it in when it ends. Results are summarized here and
written up in [README.md](README.md) or [research.md](research.md); raw logs are kept outside the repository.

## Plan

**Quality bar (decided 2026-10-23):** a Flint file counts only if it is within noise of Unsloth's UD-Q4_K_XL against
BF16 (KLD 0.120, 87.7 % same top token, perplexity +3.9 %; in practice KLD ≲ 0.125 and same top token ≳ 87.5 %).
People use Unsloth's quants, and nobody trades ~9 points of token agreement for speed, so files at the makers' Q4_1
level (78–80 %: makers-fast, S1, S2, the Q4_0 variants) are no longer release candidates or targets. Speed claims compare
against UD-Q4_K_XL on the same build and cards. Engine and kernel work still counts wherever it is measured, because it
speeds up every file.

## Registry

Status is **planned**, **running**, **done** or **dropped**. Quality numbers are same top token / mean KL divergence /
perplexity change against the reference named in the row, on 80 × 512 tokens of wikitext-2. Speed is real-chat tok/s on
the rig (llama.cpp `d77256999` + CUDA graphs, `-bs`, 262,144-token context) unless the row says otherwise.

Elixir models, training and model shrinking have their own repo,
[elixir-agents-on-mining-rigs](https://github.com/Cinderella-Man/elixir-agents-on-mining-rigs). Its registry,
`experiments.md`, keeps the original ids:
- the Elixir fine-tuning rows, Q472–Q492 and Q494–Q503;
- the DeepSeek-teacher rows, Q524–Q545;
- the open expert-pruning ideas: Q239, Q242, Q815, Q892, Q897, Q898, Q902, Q903, Q1141 and Q1142.

The finished expert-cut runs (Q232, Q890, Q891) stay here with their data.

New ideas of these kinds get their rows there, not here, and that registry is searched first, so no idea is found
twice:
- **Elixir and training:** fine-tuning, LoRA, distillation, RL, teacher models, task mining, Elixir models.
- **Model shrinking:** cutting or merging parts, such as expert pruning (REAP, RCO, usage cuts), expert merging (REAM,
  HC-SMoE), shared bases, layer or head drops, vocabulary trims, lottery tickets.

Run-time skipping that keeps the file whole stays here: the per-token expert skip (Q618), activation sparsity (Q622)
and the cold tier (Q238).

| Q163 | Long prompts are attention-bound: a 64k prompt reads at 67.8 tok/s on nine cards (Q116), and the rig's fills put attention at ~0.33 ms per prompt token per 1k of depth, i.e. the stock FP32 TILE kernel at ~0.7 TFLOPS (~32 % of a P106's FP32 peak). Its 2×4 / 4×4 register tiles load 0.75 and 0.5 floats from shared memory per FMA, against the 0.25 that sm_61's 32 floats per clock and SM allow. A register-tiled FP32 prompt kernel for compute 6.1 (head 128 for Flint, head 256 for the Qwen3.6 class, 8 query heads per KV head) that also reads a Q8_0 cache directly (Q61) and skips all-masked key tiles; est. attention ~1.6× faster, a 64k prompt ~68 → ~93 tok/s | in v2.0, on | Fork branch `pascal-p106-v2-prefill-attn` (`79613a54e`, on `pascal-p106-v2-next` `d379da309`; not pushed yet: its base waits for the owner's push approval): `fattn-tile-pascal.cu`, the TILE case and the F16-copy reservation in `fattn.cu`. 128 threads, 32 columns (4 tokens × 8 heads) at head 128 and 16 at head 256, 64- and 128-key tiles, 30 KiB of shared memory, 3 blocks per SM; scores 4 keys × 8 columns over half the head with a partner-lane swap at head 128 (67 % ceiling), 4 × 4 at head 256; P·V 4 columns × 8 dimensions (67 % ceiling); K/V staged in FP32 chunks one chunk ahead from F16 or Q8_0, so a Q8_0 cache needs no F16 copy (−512 MiB per card at 262k). | Q164 | A simple 2–3-bit format for Pascal, so that Ornith-1.5-122B fits 54 GB and decodes fast (owner, 2026-10-27: the new-format route over kernels for the existing IQ/K formats): why IQ2_S/IQ3_XXS are slow, prior art, candidate layouts with decode kernels and a roofline, and a CPU quality proxy on real expert weights (queue L) | done: research and proxy; the types and their tests continue in Q185–Q189 | **Today's IQ2_S/IQ3_XXS experts run 10.8/20.5 ps per weight** (v2.0 profile), gather-bound: both do ~1.4 grid lookups per SM per clock. Below ~3.5 bits the P106 is issue-bound per weight, so bits buy memory, not time; a 2–3-bit format can at best reach Q4_0's ~4.2 ps. Candidates with levels in registers decoded by byte permutes: est. 3.5–4 ps; IQ Pascal kernels with shared-memory tables (`pascal-p106-v3-iqmmvq`) measured 6.4–9.2 after two rounds of tuning (gate/up 6.67 IQ2_S, down 7.07 IQ3_XXS), so N2P/N3P est. ~1.8× faster per expert weight. **Proxy** (importance-weighted reconstruction error, 84 matrices of 7 layers): register-table levels match the IQ codebooks at equal size; ik_llama.cpp's shifted-table bit makes N2+ (2.6875 bits) / N3+ (3.25) a mix with 6 % less error than the best IQ mix of its size (2.875 bits); uniform levels and Q2_K/Q3_K +11–24 %, Hadamard rotation +9 %, mainline Q2_0 17× IQ3_XXS. Dense tensors Q8_0 → Q5_0 is the larger lever (est. −10 to −12 ms of 118). Recommendation: measure the IQ kernels on the rig, then two gates (N2+/N3+ prototype kernels in `bench/mmvq_pascal`, simulated-quantization KLD on the 35B) before building the types (~7–8 days). **The gates were dropped** (owner, 2026-10-27: skip the gates, build N2P and N3P); the real kernels' timing on the P106 (Q188) and the 122B files' KLD (Q186) take their place. N2P (= the proxy's `ik2x_s4x8`) and N3P (= `ik3x_s5x32`) are built (Q185), Ornith-1.5-122B files with them made (Q186, Q187); the P106 timing and the agent check come next (Q188, Q189) | [note](../docs/research/notes/pascal_lowbit_format.md); [data, build, test, rig and quantize scripts](../docs/data/2026-10-27_lowbit/README.md); [lowbit_proxy.py](../scripts/lowbit_proxy.py), [lowbit_summary.py](../scripts/lowbit_summary.py) |

With `RETRY_STOPPED=1` (the default; `remote.sh` passes it on) the load's files go to `OUT/stopped/<load>-<n>/`, `loads.tsv` gets a line with `stopped` in its `timed` column, `requests.csv` is rebuilt without the stopped requests, the run goes on, and the stopped loads start again at the end in the order they stopped. A second stop of one load in a run ends the run; a stopped warm-up load is not started again; `RETRY_STOPPED=0` ends the run at the first stop, as before. A stop is the watchdog's `watchdog:` line in the server log or its `KILL` in its samples, read after giving the watchdog up to 3 s to write them. `deep_table.py` reads the stop lines apart, counts a load listed twice with its last start, lists the loads in the order they ran, and names every stop in its last check (the last request answered or "while loading", the watchdog's reason, the folder, whether the load ran again). The self-test runs the real watchdog on a stand-in `/proc/meminfo`: one load stopped after its decode pass 1 at depth 512 and one while loading (the run done, 51 requests with each load once, both stops listed), one load stopped on both starts (the run ends at the second stop, the other loads having run between), and the retry off (the run ends at the first stop, files in place): 49 of 49 checks, 36 before the change; the cases both versions ran wrote the same files and the same content but for the clock. In `cpy_tensor_async` a hop is one one-block kernel on each card, with no copy, event or host wait. The source card's kernel streams the tensor in chunks (`_CHUNKS`, 8) into a ring of `_SLOTS` × `_SLOT_KB` (16 × 32 KiB) slots in mapped pinned memory and raises a sequence-number flag after `__threadfence_system()`, refilling a slot only after its acknowledgement. So the two PCIe links stream at once, which C140's one-shot mailbox (436 µs for 40 KB, the same as a host-staged copy) did not. Prompt-sized hops read on a copy stream behind the scheduler's guard (`_STREAM`); `_MAX_KB` sends them to the staged hop instead; a wait past `_TIMEOUT_MS` traps.
